title: Sealed network upgrade surgeon checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a surgeon-style checklist and working notes for performing air-gapped installs and in-place upgrades of Redwood Private in sealed VPC/on-prem environments. Focus: artifact mirroring, offline registries, dependency bundles, and Terraform module implications. This is intentionally prescriptive but pragmatic — meant for small ops teams doing manual or semi-automated upgrades where network egress is restricted.

Scope and assumptions:
- Target audience: SREs and infra engineers performing offline installs or upgrades for customers using the Redwood Private package.
- Environment type: sealed VPCs, isolated racks, or on-prem clusters with NO outbound internet.
- We assume access to a transient 'staging mirror host' with dual-homed networking (internet + secure transfer medium) used to build bundles.
- Customer operators have KMS/HSM integration for signing keys or an agreed PGP keypair for artifact signing.
- Terraform is used to deploy the customer-side operator resources; notes below outline module knobs and anti-patterns.

High-level flow (one-line):
1) intake bundle spec -> 2) build bundle on staging host -> 3) sign + verify -> 4) transport (sneakernet/airgap appliance) -> 5) seed registry/registry-proxy -> 6) apply terraform + run smoke tests -> 7) run canary rollout -> 8) full upgrade -> 9) post-upgrade validation and artifact purge.

Bundle composition (recommended):
- <release>-bundle.tar.gz (or .tar.xz for size-sensitive customers) containing:
  - manifest.json (see manifest schema below)
  - images/ (OCI images as tar archives: name_tag.tar)
  - charts/ (Helm charts tarball or raw manifests)
  - binaries/ (kube-controller, sidecars, operator binaries)
  - packages/ (rpm/deb packages if customer uses host-level installs)
  - signatures/ (manifest.sig and per-artifact sigs)

Manifest minimal schema (example fields):
- version: "2024.10"
- bundle_id: "redwood-private-2024-10-rc2"
- created_by: "staging-host-01 / team"
- created_at: "2024-10-03T14:32:00Z"
- artifacts: [ list of lines like "oci:sha256:<digest>  size  path/images/name_tag.tar  signed_by:pgp:0xAB12" ]
- tf_module_version: "private-deploy-v0.6.3"
- required_host_packages: ["containerd>=1.6","ebtables"]

Signing and verification notes:
- Prefer customer-managed KMS for final signing. If unavailable, use PGP with a verified cross-signed key exchange during onboarding.
- Sign both manifest.json and each image tar using sha256 and detached signature (gpg --detach-sign --armor manifest.json).
- Verification steps on target cluster:
  - gpg --verify manifest.json.asc manifest.json
  - for each image: sha256sum -c checksums.txt && gpg --verify <image>.asc <image>.
- Automate signature checks in the local registry seeding script to fail-fast if any signature mismatch.

Offline registry seeding (recommended pattern):
- Provide two options depending on customer constraints:
  1) Local registry import: load images directly into customer registry (e.g., crane/ctr image load -> registryctl import)
  2) Registry proxy seeding: seed a mirror registry on an appliance that proxies requests for images the first time and serves locally afterward.
- Seeding script (pseudo):
  - extract bundle
  - verify signatures
  - for image in images/: ctr image import --digest <sha> image.tar && ctr image tag <digest> registry.local/repo:tag && skopeo copy docker-archive:image.tar docker://registry.local/repo:tag
  - push charts to local chartmuseum if charts exist

Terraform module notes (design constraints & anti-patterns):
- Module inputs we recommend exposing to customers:
  - mirror_bucket_name (string) - remote staging bucket used for bundle composition
  - local_registry_host (string) - host:port for customer registry
  - registry_tls_mode (string) - [self_signed|customer_ca|public_ca]
  - auth_mode (string) - [none|basic|token|mtls]
  - operator_image_override (map of strings) - allow pinning of images loaded into the cluster
  - bundle_manifest_path (string) - path on cluster/op appliance to load manifest from
- Helpful outputs: bundle_applied_checksum, registry_import_log_url (if appliance has web UI), deployed_operator_version
- Anti-patterns to avoid in module design:
  - Embedding external network fetch logic inside the TF module (don’t let apply try to reach the internet). Keep TF to create resources and call local execs that operate on pre-seeded artifacts.
  - Overly permissive IAM roles for mirror hosts—use least privilege S3 roles and scoped service accounts for upload/download.
- Example Terraform snippet (pseudo):
  module "private_deploy" {
    source = "github.com/redwood-infra/terraform-modules//private-deploy"
    local_registry_host = var.local_registry_host
    registry_tls_mode = var.registry_tls_mode
    operator_image_override = var.operator_image_override
    bundle_manifest_path = "/opt/bundle/manifest.json"
  }

Upgrade strategy (minor vs major):
- Minor patch (operator or sidecar < 1.0 semver minor):
  - Use canary by node pool or namespace.
  - Steps: seed images -> apply manifests to isolated namespace -> monitor for 30 minutes -> promote.
- Minor version (backwards compatible feature):
  - Run schema/compatibility smoke tests against canary namespace. If passing, proceed to phased rollout across namespaces.
- Major version (breaking change):
  - Do not auto-upgrade. Require offline-runbook-approved plan.
  - Create a rollback bundle and locally test migration on a non-prod mirrored cluster before touching prod.

Canary policy for sealed envs (constraints-driven):
- Use 1-2 canary nodes (smallest footprint) with full telemetry enabled.
- Define SLOs to validate: startup-time < 45s, p95 request-latency delta < 10% versus baseline, error-rate < 0.5% additional errors.
- If any SLO fails, auto-block the rest of the rollout and capture traces/logs to an encrypted bundle for offline triage.

Rollback plan (must be rehearsed):
- Keep the previous operator images and manifests in the bundle repository and on the appliance until 72 hours after successful full rollout.
- Rollback steps:
  - Apply previous manifests from rollback bundle -> monitor canary -> slowly scale back to 100% if healthy.
  - If data migrations ran during upgrade, have schema-reversion scripts tested on staging.

Validation and smoke tests (local):
- Basic connectivity: kubelet -> registry.local pull test, controller manager start, readiness probes pass
- Functional smoke: generate a 100-request synthetic load against canary endpoint, compare outputs to baseline via golden prompts stored in bundle/tests/golden.json
- Security checks: run offline vulnerability scanner against images (trivy --input image.tar --format json) and include output inside bundle/scan-report.json

Operational automation (helper scripts suggestions):
- build_bundle.sh --release <version> --include-charts --sign --output /tmp/bundle.tar.gz
- seed_registry.sh --bundle /tmp/bundle.tar.gz --registry registry.local:5000 --verify-sigs
- tf-apply-offline.sh -> copies bundle to appliance, runs terraform init/plan/apply with local exec triggers to run seeding scripts.

Testing before transport (critical checks):
- All artifacts present and checksums recorded in manifest.json.
- All signatures valid using designated key.
- A minimal local k3s cluster on staging should be able to consume the bundle end-to-end (deploy operator, create test workload).
- Smoke test logs archived and attached to bundle as tests/smoke.log.

Transport and staging guidance:
- Prefer encrypted disk images transferred via appliance. Use rsync --archive --compress --progress --partial over a physically moved drive for reliability.
- For high-security customers: use HSM-backed signing and include a chain-of-custody file indicating who handled the media and timestamped hashes.

Unresolved questions / decisions to make:
- Should we standardize on PGP or require KMS for signing in all enterprise contracts? Pros/cons in appendix.
- Should Terraform modules expose an automated 'seed_and_apply' boolean that runs seeding scripts from the appliance via ssh? (Security tradeoffs)
- Migration testing: do we provide a reference appliance image for customers to run tests locally, or ship a lightweight test harness only?

Appendix: quick commands (examples)
- Create checksums manifest: find images -type f -exec sha256sum {} \; > checksums.txt
- Sign manifest: gpg --armor --detach-sign --output manifest.json.asc manifest.json
- Verify sample image: sha256sum -c checksums.txt && gpg --verify images/my-operator.tar.asc images/my-operator.tar
- Load image into containerd: ctr -n=k8s.io images import images/my-operator.tar
- Push to local registry via skopeo: skopeo copy docker-archive:images/my-operator.tar docker://registry.local/repo:tag

Notes to self / next steps:
- Draft a small reference terraform module that keeps all network fetches out of the apply path and exposes hooks for local-exec seeding. (Connor to own prototype)
- Create a canonical bundle validator script that produces a single exit code and standardized report (Marta prototype).
- Work with security to finalize signing policy (Devon to coordinate with legal for contract language).

End of document.
